title: Rework ingress fragmentation smoothing and function-call throttle adjustments
author: Asha Mehta
ci_status: pass (flaky integration re-run after timeout fix)
release_notes: Tightens default payload limits for streaming endpoints; improves streaming stability for function/tool calls by smoothing ingress fragments and lowering writer backpressure thresholds. No API contract changes for customers; opt-in knobs available for enterprise routes.
description:
Context and motivation: We continue to see latency spikes and incorrect structured outputs for function calls under mixed-size workloads. Root causes traced to bursty ingress fragments (large client frames followed by tiny ones), aggressive proxy writer wakeups, and the OpenAI-compat streaming path buffering incomplete fncall JSON across fragment boundaries. Goal: reduce tail latency and reduce malformed fncall outputs without changing external API semantics.

Summary of changes: consolidates three related areas into a single PR so rollout is atomic: 1) Ingress fragmentation smoother: a small stateful coalescer in the gateway that groups incoming TCP/frame fragments into 128KB smoothing windows, emitting a steady stream to the proxy rather than bursts. This reduces head-of-line variability for downstream batching. 2) Function-call specific buffering: OpenAI-compat streaming path now defers final fncall object emission until the entire structured payload is validated (content-length / JSON-closure heuristics). This fixes cases where toolbackends received partial JSON and returned 400s that surprised clients. 3) Backpressure/threshold tuning: proxy_writer thresholds lowered for streaming routes with fncall enabled (writer_wakeup_ms from 12 -> 8ms, fragment_ack_window reduced to 3 frames) and route crediting logic adjusted to favor small-payload low-latency routes.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for coalescer boundaries and small/large frames - [x] Integration test reproducing previous malformed fncall bug - [x] Load test showing tail-p99 latency improvement on mixed workloads - [x] Documentation note in gateway config schema for new knobs - [x] Manual canary in east-1 with limited routes

Commits (high level): - add: ingress smoothing coalescer and config knobs (ash/ingress_coalesce.go) - fix: openai-compat fncall stream finalizer (compat/stream/fncall_finalizer.go) - tweak: proxy writer thresholds and route-crediting (proxy/writer.go, router/policy.go) - test: integration/flaky-fncall-repro and unit tests - docs: gateway-config.md additions

Files changed (high level): - gateway/ingress_coalesce.go (new) - compat/stream/fncall_finalizer.go (new) - proxy/writer.go (modified) - router/policy.go (modified) - tests/integration/fncall_stream_repro_test.go (new) - docs/gateway-config.md (modified)

Behavioral notes for operators: default behavior is opt-in per-route via route.config.ingress_coalesce (default: true for streaming+fncall routes). New knobs: ingress_coalesce_window_bytes (default 131072), writer_wakeup_ms (default 8 for streaming), fragment_ack_window (default 3). Enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private can override globally via deployment flags. No changes to API request/response formats; OpenAI-compat framing (data: ... chunks and [DONE]) remains unchanged, but chunk emission timing is smoother.

Backwards compatibility & risk: This is non-breaking. Risk vector: the coalescer could increase per-request latency for ultra-low-volume micro-requests if misconfigured. Mitigation: default window is small (128KB) and we added a fast-path that bypasses coalescer for sub-4KB stable sessions. Canary rollout plan in the PR: enable for 10% of streaming fncall routes -> 40% -> 100% over 48 hours with automated rollback on p99 increase > 20%.

Testing and results: Local unit tests: 100% pass. Integration: reproduced prior fncall partial-JSON bug and verified fixed. Loadbench: mixed-size workload (40% small chat tokens, 60% long context streaming with fncall) showed p50 unchanged, p95 -12%, p99 -18% in east-1 canary cluster. One regression noted: a low-frequency CI unit flake in router/policy_tests (timing-based); fixed by making test tolerant of ±5ms scheduling jitter.

Review conversation: "Diego Ramos" (reviewer) - comment: "Ingress coalescer looks good but please add a metric for dropped/queued bytes so we can monitor backpressure." Asha - reply: "Added gauge gateway.ingress.coalescer.queued_bytes and a health alert in docs; pushed new commit." "Lina Park" - comment: "Why lower writer_wakeup_ms? could increase CPU spin." Asha - reply: "Lowered because we observed writer latency dominating small-payload routes; the coalescer lowers burst frequency so lowering wakeup is net CPU-neutral in tests. Added a toggle and benchmark numbers in the PR." "Samir Gupta" - approval: "Approach seems sound; canary plan OK."

CI and merges: Initial CI run failed on a flaky integration test (router timing). I reworked the test and re-ran CI; all checks passed. Merge method: squash and merge. Merge commit: "Rework ingress fragmentation smoothing and function-call throttle adjustments (squashed)".

Rollback and follow-ups: Rollback criteria and automated canary thresholds added to monitoring playbook. Follow-ups: (1) evaluate window sizing heuristics per-tenant in Dedicated (ENG-4301), (2) extend smoothing to websockets ingress path (ENG-4334), (3) audit route-matching rules for small-payload preference to avoid starvation.

Notes to docs/SDK teams: No API changes; SDKs may observe slightly fewer partial fncall errors for streaming calls, please call out the stability improvement in release notes.

References: Linear ENG-4212 (investigation), SUP-1198 (customer incident), related PRs: none directly touch same files but conceptually adjacent to previous gateway tweaks (see history for proxy writer tuning).
